user.title: Add a Companion server
user.description: Enter the address of the computer running Bitfocus Companion. The port is Companion's satellite port (Settings > Protocols > Satellite listen port, 16622 by default).

error.cannot_connect: Could not reach Companion's satellite port. Check the address and that Companion is running.
error.unknown: Unexpected error. See the Home Assistant log.

abort.already_configured: This Companion server is already set up.
abort.already_in_progress: This Companion server is already being set up.

add_button.title: Add a Companion button
add_button.description: Pick a button by its position in Companion. Rows and columns start at 0; pages start at 1. The same button keeps working on your Stream Deck.

scan_page.title: Scan a Companion page
scan_page.description: Fallback when Companion's admin API cannot be read: Home Assistant subscribes to every position on the page (up to 8 rows by 16 columns) and lists the ones with something on them.

pick_buttons.title: Choose buttons
pick_buttons.description: {count} buttons found. Tick the ones to add. Each is named after its button text; you can rename the entities afterwards.

http_settings.title: Companion HTTP API
http_settings.description: Variables are read over Companion's HTTP API, which runs on the same port as Companion's web interface (8000 by default). Companion listens on localhost only unless you change the interface in the Companion launcher window; choose all interfaces (0.0.0.0) there if you can. Leave the host empty to use {host}, the address the satellite connection uses, or enter the address Companion's web interface listens on. Home Assistant tests the address before saving.

add_variables_by_name.title: Add Companion variables by name
add_variables_by_name.description: Pick the connection, then paste variable names one per line (or label:name / $(label:name) to mix connections). Copy names from Companion's Variables tab. Each becomes a sensor. Give a unit (for example dB) to get numeric sensors with graphs.

add_variables.title: Add Companion variables
add_variables.description: Choose which connection's variables to browse. Companion's own Home Assistant connection can have thousands, so type part of a name or description to narrow the list first.

pick_variables.title: Choose variables
pick_variables.description: {count} variables on {label} (filter: {filter}), shown with their current values. Type to search, tick the ones to add. Give a unit such as dB when the values are numbers.

entity_settings.title: Entity settings
entity_settings.description: Each chosen Companion button is one button entity whose attributes carry the live text, colours and pressed state. A text sensor adds text history. Button images add an image entity per button showing its face exactly as Companion draws it (meters and all), refreshed on every redraw; the button's image_entity attribute names it.

data.button_sensors: Also create a text sensor for each button
data.button_images: Also create an image of each button as Companion draws it

add_buttons.title: Add Companion buttons
add_buttons.description: {count} of Companion's {total} buttons are not in Home Assistant yet (page navigation buttons are left out). Tick the ones to add. Each is named after its text; rotary buttons also get rotate left and rotate right entities.

error.not_connected: Home Assistant is not connected to this Companion server right now.
error.subscriptions_disabled: Companion's Button Subscriptions API is switched off. Enable it under Settings > Protocols in Companion.
error.cannot_connect: Companion did not answer while scanning. Try again.
error.nothing_found: No buttons with text or colour on that page. Check the page number and grid size.
error.http_unreachable: Companion's HTTP API did not answer at {url}. Check the host and port, and that Companion's launcher is set to listen on that address (or all interfaces) rather than localhost.
error.invalid_variable: Could not read these as variable names: {missing}. Use label:name, for example RCV:combo1_livelevelL.
error.variables_not_found: Companion does not know these variables: {missing}. Check the spelling in Companion's Variables tab.
error.catalog_unavailable: Could not read the variable list from Companion's admin API at {url}. Check the HTTP API settings, or use 'Add variables by name'.
error.nothing_matched: No variables on {label} match the filter '{filter}'.
error.too_many: {count} variables on {label} is too many to list. Type part of a name in the filter to narrow it down.
error.nothing_missing: Every Companion button is already in Home Assistant.

subscriptions_disabled.title: Enable button subscriptions in Companion
subscriptions_disabled.description:
Home Assistant is connected to {name} ({host}), but Companion's **Button Subscriptions API** is switched off, so buttons cannot be pressed or watched from here.

In Companion open **Settings > Protocols** and turn on **Enable Button Subscriptions API**. Home Assistant reconnects on its own.

companion_too_old.title: Companion is too old for this integration
companion_too_old.description: {name} ({host}) is running Companion {version}. Button subscriptions need Companion 4.3 or newer. Update Companion, then reload the integration.

http_unreachable.title: Companion's HTTP API is not reachable
http_unreachable.description:
Variables for {name} are read from http://{host}:{port}/api, but it did not answer, so the variable sensors are unavailable.

Companion listens on localhost only by default. In the Companion launcher window change the interface it listens on to the computer's network address (or all interfaces), or correct the port under the integration's **Configure → HTTP API settings**.

pages_unavailable.title: Companion's page map is not reachable
pages_unavailable.description:
Home Assistant follows Companion buttons by their stable id when you move them between positions or pages, using Companion's admin API at http://{host}:{port}. That API did not answer for {name}, so buttons are tracked by position only until it is back: a moved button would stop updating until you re-add it.

Check the HTTP API settings under the integration's Configure menu, and that Companion's launcher listens on an address Home Assistant can reach.
